To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dimensionless roof extension length, dimensionless offshore leakage, and tidal amplitude affect the groundwater level fluctuation in a leaky confined multilayer aquifers; and (2) the dimensionless inland leakage affects the fluctuation only when the roof is extended under the sea.
the groundwater level fluctuation in a confined aquifer under the sea decreases significantly with the length of the roof, which extends under the sea, and increases with the tidal efficiency.

the groundwater level fluctuation in a multilayer aquifersystem is significantly influenced by the dimensionless roof extension, the dimensionless leakage, the tidal efficiency, and the ratio of the leakage from the inland to that from the offshore portions of the confine unit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the groundwater response to tidal fluctuations in a coastal multiaquifer system.
the effect of the roof extension under the sea and the leakage from the confining unit on the groundwater response to tidal fluctuations in a multilayer coastal aquifer system.
the impact of the roof length of the confined aquifers, leakage from the confined unit, and tidal efficiency of the sea on groundwater level fluctuation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a leaky confined coastal aquifer with a roof extending under the sea behaves differently from an aquifer that does not extend under the sea, especially in terms of the groundwater fluctuation.

the roof extension, leakage from the offshore portion, and tidal efficiency all tend to increase the fluctuating amplitude of the groundwater level in the inland part, while the leakage from the inland confining unit tends to decrease the amplitude of the fluctuation.

the groundwater level in a coastal leak aquifer system is more likely to be affected by the offshore portion of the roof than by the inland portion of the roof, and the groundwater level fluctuation is more likely to increase as the tidal efficiency and the offshore leakage increase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the groundwater fluctuation in the confined aquifer system depends not only on the aquifer parameters but also on the tidal efficiency.
the roof length of the leaky aquifer system is a key factor in the tidal response of groundwater in the inland part, and it is necessary to take it into account in the analysis.
, in order to understand groundwater level fluctuations in a coastal aquifer, the roof length and the leakages from both the offshore and inland sides of the confining layer should be considered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the groundwater response to tidal forcing is sensitive to the roof length and the leakage from the confining unit.

the roof length, leakage from the confined aquifer, and tidal efficiency are all important factors in determining the groundwater level fluctuations, which should be taken into consideration in the analysis of groundwater response to tides.
the roof of a coastal aquifer extending under the sea has significant impact on the groundwater fluctuation in the confined aquifer, especially when the roof length of the confined aquifers is short.
